items.title: Study quantifies how often women with low desire still have sex out of obligation
items.summary: A study in the Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy by Nikita Guptan and James A. Simon (IntimMedicine Specialists) found that women with chronic low sexual desire still had sex with partners roughly two to three times a month even before any treatment, often motivated by relationship obligation rather than personal arousal. The authors argue this 'baseline' of obligatory sex complicates how clinical trials measure the success of new low-desire treatments.
items.sowhat: A validating, destigmatizing stat for anyone who's had sex to keep the peace rather than out of desire, a great springboard for content about consent, communication, and treating low desire as real and common.
items.caption: New study: women with low desire still have sex an average of 2-3x a month, often just to stay close to a partner. Translation: your desire is valid, and so is talking about it 💬
items.source: PsyPost (covering Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy)

items.title: Openness to diverse sexual practices linked to better sexual well-being
items.summary: A study published in the journal Psychology & Sexuality found that young adults with open, favorable attitudes toward specific sexual practices reported higher sexual pleasure, satisfaction, self-esteem, and confidence. The researchers frame this openness as a protective factor and argue sex education should move away from a purely risk-focused model.
items.sowhat: Hard science backing what Nancy already believes: curiosity and openness about pleasure are good for you, which is a perfect hook for destigmatizing content.
items.caption: New research says the more open-minded you are about what turns you on, the better sex feels. Curiosity really is the sexiest trait 💫

items.title: Couples searching for a third partner report stronger bonds
items.summary: A qualitative study in Psychology & Sexuality, led by Alena Bondarchuk-Mclaughlin at La Trobe University, found that couples who went looking together for a third partner often became more connected and improved their communication as a pair. The researchers also noted couples tended to center their own pleasure and underweight the prospective third person's wishes.
items.sowhat: Validating, inclusive content for non-monogamy-curious followers: exploring together can genuinely strengthen a couple, with a built-in reminder to keep everyone's needs equally in the mix.
items.caption: New research: couples who go searching for a third together often come back closer than ever 💘 (Scientist tip: make sure everyone's wishes get equal billing.)

items.title: Meta's Ad Policy Goes Claims-Based for Sexual Health
items.summary: In late July 2026 Meta rewrote its Health & Wellness advertising standards, replacing blanket category rejections with claim-by-claim review, so ads for sexual health, wellness, and reproductive products can run if each individual claim complies. Ads that are overtly sexual, pleasure-focused, or use close-up body-part imagery remain banned under the revised standard.
items.sowhat: Audit Nancy's Meta ad copy and creative line-by-line for compliant wellness framing instead of assuming the whole category is blocked — clean claims can now get approved.
items.caption: Plot twist from Meta: it's not about what you sell anymore, it's about what you say. Claims > categories now. More honest wellness talk, zero clickbait — that's our whole vibe anyway. 💬✨

items.title: France's Under-15 Social Media Ban Struck Down Over Weak Age-Verification Safeguards
items.summary: On August 14, 2026, France's Constitutional Council struck down the country's new under-15 social media ban, ruling it disproportionate because the law failed to adequately protect privacy in how age verification would be carried out. France's separate mandatory age-verification regime for adult/pornographic sites (the SREN law) was not touched by this ruling and remains in force, having been upheld by the EU's top court in June 2026.
items.sowhat: Correct the record internally — France paused the youth ban for a rewrite, but did NOT relax adult age-gating; keep any France-facing adult-content verification flows exactly as they are.
items.caption: France just sent its under-15 social media ban back to the drawing board — but grown-up age checks for adult content? Still very much the law of the land. Safety for every age bracket, done right. 🇫🇷🔐

items.title: TikTok Shop Tightens 'Sexualized Behavior' Rules for Sellers and Creators
items.summary: On August 4, 2026, TikTok Shop published a new 'Prohibited Content for Platform Safety' policy for US sellers and creators, explicitly barring nudity and sexualized behavior in shoppable videos and LIVEs alongside stronger minor-protection rules. The policy applies regardless of a seller's intent or target audience, so even wellness-framed content can be flagged if it reads as sexualized.
items.sowhat: Keep Nancy's TikTok Shop videos and LIVEs strictly product-education framed with zero innuendo, since the rule applies no matter what audience you're actually trying to reach.
items.caption: TikTok Shop just drew a brighter line around 'sexualized' content — intent doesn't matter, vibe does. We'll keep our LIVEs informative, playful, and policy-proof. 💡🛍️
